## EQUATORIAL GUINEA — profile (page 155)

- **Header facts:** Region: Sub-Saharan Africa; Income group: Upper-middle-income; Lending category: IBRD; Data status: Data as reported (A); Population: 1.9 million; GNI: 11,611; Unit: US$ million, unless otherwise indicated.
- **Total external debt stock 2025:** 1,103, **-9.6% from 2024**.
- **Figure 1. Total external debt, 2019–25:** 2019 = **1,515**; 2025 = **1,103**. The line falls from 2019 to ≈2020, rises to a local peak at ≈2021, is nearly flat/slightly lower at ≈2022, then declines through ≈2023 and ≈2024 to 2025. Highest printed point is **2019 (1,515)**; the series ends lower in 2025.
- **Figure 2. External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:**
  - **Total external debt:** 1,103
  - **Public & publicly guaranteed (PPG):** 1,103
  - **Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type:** 1,103
    - **Multilateral:** 384
    - **Bilateral:** 719
  - **Multilateral (total):** 384
    - **IMF-SDR allocations:** 250
    - **AfDB:** 69
    - **Other multilateral:** 66
  - **Bilateral (total):** 719
    - **China:** 719
  - **Private creditors / PNG / short-term:** no values shown on the page.
- **Figure 3. Debt ratios, 2019–25:**
  - **External debt / exports:** 40%, **+82.7%**; visible line rises overall to 2023.  
  - **External debt / GNI:** 10%, **-8.1%**; line trends downward overall from 2019 to 2025 with a small mid-period uptick.
  - **Debt service / exports:** 5%, **+82.7%**; visible line rises, dips, then rises again to 2023.
  - **Debt service / GNI:** 2%, **+5.2%**; line falls early, then fluctuates slightly and is roughly flat by 2025.
- **Figure 4. Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025:**
  - **Official creditors:** Maturity **25 yrs**; Grace period **8 yrs**; Interest rate **1.2%**
  - **Private creditors:** Maturity **..**; Grace period **..**; Interest rate **..**
- **Notes/Source:**
  - *Source:* World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
  - *Note:* Figure 3 shows no data values for the exports-based ratios after 2023.
  - *Note:* Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
